segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Hello, everybody and welcome to this informal meeting about the University Helpline.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The Helpline was set up ten years ago by the Students Union and it aims to provide new students to the university with a service that they can use if they need information about practical areas of student life that they are unfamiliar with.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Let me give you some examples of the type of help we can offer.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We can provide information on financial matters; for , you may feel that your grant is insufficient to see you through college life or you may have some queries regarding the fees you are paying if you are an overseas student.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: In both cases, the Helpline would be able to go through things with you and see what the outcome might be.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Another area we can help with is what we generally term the ‘domestic’ area; things such as childcare and the availability of nursery provision, for , come under this.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then there’s ‘academic’ issues that may arise while you are in the early stages of your course that you may not know what to do about.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: You may wish to know more about essay deadlines, for , or how to use the library - there are all kinds of questions you will find yourself asking and not knowing where to get quick answers from.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The Helpline would be able to provide these.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The last I’ve given here is simply termed ‘social’ - and yes, there is a lot of social life here!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But you may have a particular interest you wish to pursue or you may wish to participate in outings or trips if you don’t know many people at the moment. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Let me give you some details so that you know where to go and who to see if you want to pay us a visit.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Generally you will see our Helpline officer Jackie Kouachi, that’s K-O-U-A- C-H-I.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Jackie is a full-time employee of the Student Union and she works in the Student Welfare Office - that’s the office that deals with all matters related to student welfare and it’s located at 13 Marshall Road.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I have some maps here for those of you who haven’t been there yet.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you wish to ring the office, the number is 326 99 40.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The office is open between 9.30 and 6.00 on weekdays and from 10 to 4 on Saturdays and Tipescripts there’ll be somebody there - usually Jackie or myself - between those times.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: If you want to make an appointment you can phone or call at the office in person.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Please note that it may not be possible for anyone to see you straight away - particularly if it is a busy time - lunch time for - and you may have to go on the waiting list and then come back later.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, enough from me.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Any questions?
